title: PV22: a Setapak stalwart designs for its customers' parents.
excerpt: Two towers of 2,082 units above developer-owned retail beside a future MRT3 station, designed for older residents. Sean praises the step-free design and the larger units, but flags the density and Setapak's traffic.
takeaways: Units from 480 to 1,300 sq ft; the 1,300 sq ft three-bedroom starts at about RM800,000.
The developer keeps the 55 retail units, planned around wellness, eldercare and clinics.
Step-free from drop-off to bathroom, but 2,082 units in a dense, congested area.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: PV22 is two towers of 2,082 units on 6 acres above two floors of retail, with 25 units and ten lifts per floor. The developer is keeping all 55 retail units and plans a wellness focus with an eldercare day centre and clinics, and it designs for older residents: rollover kerbs and no steps from the drop-off to the bedrooms, a reflexology garden and herb plots on a deck with a 50 m pool and indoor basketball court.

Units run from 480 sq ft to 1,300 sq ft. Sean viewed the largest, a three-bedroom, three-bathroom unit with a 3 m ceiling, a large yard, a 5.8 m-wide living area, a 1.2 by 3.6 m balcony and a 2.1 m-wide step-free master bathroom. A 1,000 sq ft unit is shown with a treatment room, a hobby room and an oversized bathroom.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: The site sits off Jalan Genting Klang beside PV21, a short walk from the future Setapak station on the MRT3 line, with Jalan Pahang and MRR2 leading to KLCC. Wangsa Maju LRT, TAR UMT, a Giant hypermarket, Columbia Asia hospital and the developer's own retail strips with Aeon Big, McDonald's and Starbucks are nearby, among many of the developer's earlier PV blocks.

standout.title: Step-free from car to shower
standout.body: Kerbs roll over at the drop-off, the deck and the unit entrance use gentle 1 in 12 ramps, and even the master bathroom has no step. Sean thinks every developer should adopt it, whether you push a wheelchair, a pram or a trolley, and the 2.1 m bathroom also makes bathing a baby easier.

pros: The location: Setapak's short run to KLCC via Jalan Genting Klang or MRR2, with TAR UMT and the early Wangsa Maju LRT station creating a community whose graduates settle here.
The developer's track record in Setapak: decades of PV, MH Platinum, J and Vista projects with few complaints, and now a move into placemaking, commercial spaces and a wider range of products.

Its willingness to change: keeping the retail rather than selling it, aiming at older residents with step-free design and greener facilities, and reworking layouts into bigger yards, dining areas and bathrooms, at a price where two related families might buy a large unit and a studio in the same development.
cons: Density: 2,082 units is the norm in Setapak, so compare the lift ratio and facilities rather than the unit count. Rents of PV21 next door are a fair guide to returns.
The mixed development: if the retail succeeds, visitors and double parking will cause congestion for residents, though there are three entrances.
Old-address traffic: narrow roads and a main road into the city controlled by traffic lights mean jams in and out of Setapak, which is why the developer aims for a self-sustaining development.

closing: A value-minded developer moving towards older and multi-generation buyers without abandoning affordable pricing.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this January 2026 episode and its video description. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. The developer's team showed Sean the sales gallery and show units; the starting price is theirs. Sean is an alumnus of TAR UMT nearby. Parking is limited to one or two bays per unit, so buyers should check theirs.
